title: Spire and Wolf
premise: Zephyrine Thornbury has spent twenty-two years in Hollowmere, a valley where magic cannot follow, hiding the beast-speech that would see them burned. When crown riders breach the valley hunting the gifted, Zephyrine flees with a wounded wolf who carries a message from the true king—imprisoned inside his own body by a usurper wearing his face. Guided by the wolf and hunted across a hardening winter, Zephyrine must choose between vanishing forever and unbinding the king before the usurper's armies crush the free cities. In the end, Zephyrine pays the price of survival itself: they give up their gift to break the binding, saving the realm but losing the voice that made them whole—and finding, in the silence, a belonging they never expected.
about_author: Tamsin Dunmore is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to animals she could not answer. She writes fantasy about outsiders, wild places, and the bargains we make to stay alive.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. We meet Hollowmere, where magic dies at the ridgeline, and Zephyrine's quiet double life: healer's apprentice by day, secret speaker to the valley's animals by night. A crow warns them of riders on the north road. Emotional beat: the fragile comfort of a life built on concealment.

chapters.title: Riders in Grey
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Crown soldiers arrive with a proclamation: all beast-speakers are traitors to be taken alive. The village elder trades names for mercy, and Zephyrine's mentor is seized. Emotional beat: betrayal by the community that was never truly theirs.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Carried
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Fleeing through the pass, Zephyrine finds a dying wolf shot with a silver-cored bolt—the first magic to enter the valley in generations. The wolf speaks: it bears a message from King Aldric, bound within his own body. Emotional beat: terror transforming into reluctant purpose.

chapters.title: The Price of the Pass
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. To save the wolf, Zephyrine must carry it beyond the ridge into magic's reach, surrendering the valley's protection forever. They heal it with borrowed power and feel their gift deepen dangerously. Emotional beat: grief for the self that can never go home.

chapters.title: Road of Ash
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The lowlands are burning; the usurper Queen Vessane purges the gifted ahead of her march on the free cities. Zephyrine witnesses a purge at a market town and nearly reveals themselves saving a child. Emotional beat: the cost of staying invisible while others burn.

chapters.title: The Free City of Marrowgate
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Refugees choke Marrowgate's gates. Zephyrine meets Sable, a smuggler who moves the hunted out of Vessane's reach—for a price. Distrust sparks an uneasy alliance. Emotional beat: learning that survival can be shared rather than solitary.

chapters.title: A Parliament of Rats
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Through the city's rats, Zephyrine's gift becomes known to Sable, who sees opportunity and, unexpectedly, kinship. Sable agrees to guide them toward the king's hidden loyalists. Emotional beat: two loners negotiating trust.

chapters.title: The Loyalist Cellar
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In a cellar beneath a tannery, exiled knights reveal the truth: Aldric lives, enthralled by a binding woven from his own crown, while Vessane wears his face via glamour. Only a beast-speaker can reach the animal-bound anchor of the spell. Emotional beat: awe and dread at being indispensable.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Warrens
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Vessane's witch-hunters raid the cellar. Zephyrine calls every rat, dog, and pigeon in the warrens to cover the escape—a display of power that paints a target on them. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: Wanted
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Zephyrine's face goes up on bounty boards. Sable must decide whether selling them out would fund the smuggling network or destroy everything Sable secretly believes in. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against old survival instincts.

chapters.title: The Wolf's Name
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. On the road north, the wolf finally shares its name—Fen—and its history as the king's hound, bound alongside him. Their bond deepens into something like family. Emotional beat: belonging found between species.

chapters.title: Winter Court
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The loyalists infiltrate Vessane's winter court disguised as servants. Zephyrine, posing as a mute scullery hand, comes face to face with the false king—and hears, beneath the glamour, Aldric screaming. Emotional beat: horror and compassion entwined.

chapters.title: The Anchor Beneath
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Following Fen's memory, Zephyrine discovers the binding's anchor: a chained stag kept starving in the royal menagerie, its suffering feeding the spell. Emotional beat: cold clarity about what must be done.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Gate
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A loyalist captain sells them out to save his own sons. Sable takes the blame and is captured, buying Zephyrine time to flee with the plan intact. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the truest form of belonging.

chapters.title: Alone With the Storm
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Hiding in the blizzard-buried menagerie, Zephyrine speaks with the caged beasts and confronts their oldest fear—that using their gift fully will consume them. Fen refuses to let them face it alone. Emotional beat: despair answered by devotion.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Midwinter night: Zephyrine frees the stag and pours their gift into unraveling the binding, feeling their beast-speech tear away strand by strand. Aldric wakes in his own body as Vessane's glamour shatters mid-address to her armies. Emotional beat: transcendence through loss.

chapters.title: Two Kings, One Crown
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The court erupts; Aldric, weak but himself, denounces Vessane. She escapes with her elite guard as loyalist forces and free-city militias converge on the capital. Emotional beat: justice beginning, not finished.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Broken Bridge
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, freed during the chaos. Sable leads smugglers and refugees in holding the river bridge against Vessane's army so Aldric's forces can flank. Emotional beat: the lawless becoming the realm's defenders.

chapters.title: Vessane's Last Bargain
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Cornered, Vessane offers Zephyrine their gift restored if they help her vanish. Zephyrine refuses—some prices are worth paying—and delivers her to Aldric's judgment. Emotional beat: integrity over wholeness.

chapters.title: Judgment Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Aldric, wary of vengeance dressed as justice, lets the freed cities try Vessane themselves. Zephyrine testifies not as accuser but as witness. Emotional beat: justice as something built, not imposed.

chapters.title: Silence and Song
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Giftless, Zephyrine grieves the lost voice—until they realize they still understand animals' body language, habits, and hearts, learned over a lifetime. Fen stays. Sable stays. Belonging was never the gift; it was always them. Emotional beat: mourning resolved into acceptance.

chapters.title: Spire and Wolf
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, epilogue. Spring: Aldric offers Zephyrine a place founding a sanctuary where the gifted and the hunted can live openly. From the spire balcony, Zephyrine watches Fen run the meadow below—not commanded, simply choosing to return. Emotional beat: home, finally chosen.
